title: Classic DMZ Architecture
description: A Mermaid flowchart showing the classic two-firewall DMZ design: an untrusted internet zone, a semi-trusted DMZ with public-facing hosts, and a trusted internal network, with legitimate flows in blue and a blocked attacker pivot in red.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: cybersecurity

learningObjectives: Identify the three zones of a classic DMZ design and the trust level of each.
Explain why two firewalls with deny-by-default policies contain a compromised DMZ host.
Trace which traffic flows are permitted and which are blocked.
educational.prerequisites: Basic understanding of firewalls, ports, and IP networking.

pedagogical.interaction: Static color-coded diagram with a legend; scales responsively to container width.
pedagogical.assessment: Lesson plan asks students to reason about blast radius if a DMZ host is compromised.
pedagogical.misconceptions: Counters the idea that one perimeter firewall is enough by showing the inner firewall's role.

chapter_title: "Network Security Foundations: Protocols, Firewalls, and Detection"
